Task Management · Enterprise Guide

Task Management

Coordinate scoped ERP work with projects, tasks, milestones, approvals, SLA follow-up, automation, and audit evidence while preserving tenant isolation and company separation.

Overview

Task Management owns operational tasks for the active tenant. It can track standalone work or follow-ups created by other modules, such as Garments Merchandising. Access the workspace at Task Management Home.

Current task statuses are To Do, In Progress, In Review, Done, and Cancelled. Current priorities are Low, Medium, High, and Critical.

Tenant And Company Scope

Tenant identity is resolved from the signed-in session and is never supplied by task request payloads. Company is the only Task Management business scope below tenant and is validated by the platform access guards before records are listed, created, changed, automated, exported, or replayed.

  • Company-scoped users see only companies they can access.
  • Projects, tasks, milestones, templates, SLA policies, webhooks, automation rules, assignment rules, delegations, evidence exports, and audit entries are scoped.
  • Cross-company dependencies, saved views, automation, and delegation are not supported by default.
  • Branch separation is intentionally out of scope for Task Management to keep operational ownership simple.

Dashboard

The dashboard summarizes scoped work: total active tasks, active projects, in-progress tasks, overdue tasks, due today, and status distribution. Counts always reflect the current tenant and selected company.

Use Quick Access to open projects, all tasks, your assigned tasks, or the calendar view.

Projects

Projects group related tasks and define default status, allowed statuses, labels, custom fields, members, and access mode. View projects at Projects.

Project scope controls the valid task scope. A project can only create tasks inside its owning company.

Workflow Policies

Enterprise workflow policies define allowed task transitions, required permissions, approval gates, and whether users must provide a reason. Configure them from the project card's Workflow action with status dropdowns, permission selection, and add/remove transition rows. Direct status changes, board movement, bulk update, and automation status changes use the same backend policy check.

Tasks

Open Tasks to work in board, list, or calendar mode. Create a new task at New Task.

Area What It Controls
Core fields Project, scope, title, description, priority, assignee, start date, due date, labels, and custom fields.
Views and filters Project, status, priority, assignee, label, milestone, linked entity, due date, overdue, and unassigned work.
Saved views Personal or company-scoped saved filters, sort order, and column preferences. Users can save the current filters, apply a view, update it, mark it default, or delete it inside the active company scope.
Bulk actions Status, assignee, and lifecycle changes for selected scoped tasks.

Lifecycle And Audit Safety

Auditable ERP work should be closed, cancelled, or archived with a reason instead of physically deleted. These actions preserve tenant, company, actor, timestamp, reason, and activity history.

Active -> Close Closed -> Archive Archived

Cancelled tasks remain available through audit and evidence views but are excluded from active task counts.

Advanced Work Management

Task details can include comments with mentions, watchers, checklist items, attachments, time logs, approvals, recurrence, dependencies, cross-links, and linked business entity metadata. Evidence export includes only scoped Task Management data plus linked entity metadata already stored on the task.

The Evidence Export page lets an authorized admin search scoped tasks, review the selected task version and scope, enter a required reason, and export the task evidence payload with a correlation ID for audit follow-up.

Templates provide reusable task defaults such as checklist items, labels, assignee rules, due offsets, custom fields, recurrence, and approval steps. Templates cannot create work outside their own tenant and scope.

Operations

SLA policies, automation rules, webhooks, reminders, and notification routing all execute inside the same tenant/company boundaries as the source tasks. Webhook replay, automation simulation, audit export, and evidence export require explicit permission for the active scope.

  • SLA policies define response and resolution expectations by project and priority.
  • Automation rules react to task events and include a read-only simulator that shows scoped task matches, matched conditions, planned actions, and skipped reasons.
  • Webhook delivery logs show status, attempts, last error, payload summary, correlation ID, and replay history. Replay requires a user-entered reason.
  • Assignment rules and delegations have dedicated admin pages for scoped create, edit, active toggle, and admin removal.
  • Assignment rules and delegations route work only inside the same tenant and allowed company scope.
